candidates.name: JB Pritzker
candidates.runningOn: Seeking a third term with running mate Christian Mitchell, a former state representative and deputy governor. His campaign points to his record on education funding, youth mental health, workforce development, climate programs, job creation, and balanced budgets, and says he will keep protecting reproductive rights and other freedoms from federal rollbacks.
candidates.priorCareer: Businessman and venture capitalist who co-founded Pritzker Group Venture Capital and the Chicago tech incubator 1871 before winning the governorship in 2018.

candidates.name: Darren Bailey
candidates.runningOn: Running a rematch of the 2022 race with running mate Aaron Del Mar after winning the March primary with about 54 percent. His campaign emphasizes affordability and property tax relief, support for working families and American jobs, protecting Second Amendment rights, and opposition to abortion.
candidates.priorCareer: Farmer and businessman from Clay County; served in the Illinois House and Senate and was the 2022 Republican nominee for governor.

candidates.name: Gary Pierce
candidates.runningOn: Running with running mate Alejandro Cabrera on the view that government should serve citizens rather than elites. His campaign emphasizes evidence-based policy, individual liberty and free speech, ending the revolving door between industry and regulators, and strengthening communities dealing with addiction and poverty.
candidates.priorCareer: Pastor with 25 years of experience in ministry and addiction recovery work.

candidates.name: Juliana Stratton
candidates.runningOn: Won the March primary over Raja Krishnamoorthi and Robin Kelly and says she is running to put middle-class families at the center of federal policy. Her campaign opposes the Trump administration's tariffs, immigration enforcement tactics, and cuts to healthcare and food assistance, and cites her seven years as lieutenant governor as preparation for the seat.
candidates.priorCareer: Lieutenant governor of Illinois since 2019; previously a state representative, justice-policy director at UIC and Cook County, and longtime president of a mediation firm.

candidates.name: Don Tracy
candidates.runningOn: Says he is running because the American Dream is slipping away for working families. His campaign focuses on lowering the cost of living, including housing, groceries, utilities, and healthcare, on public safety and support for law enforcement, on small business growth, and on representing all 102 Illinois counties rather than the Chicago area alone.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney and business leader from Springfield; former chair of the Illinois Republican Party and former chair of the Illinois Gaming Board.

candidates.name: Tyrone Muhammad
candidates.runningOn: Focuses on workforce development and job training including for returning citizens, prison reform centered on rehabilitation and education, school choice, and fiscal accountability in government. He would be the first formerly incarcerated person to appear on a statewide Illinois ballot as an independent Senate candidate.
candidates.priorCareer: Founder of Ex-Cons for Community and Social Change, a Chicago organization focused on reducing recidivism; co-founded a college-in-prison education program with the University of Illinois.

candidates.name: Kwame Raoul
candidates.runningOn: Seeking a third term as attorney general. His campaign highlights his office's work on crime and public safety, consumer and worker protections, support for crime survivors, protecting children from sexual predators, defending reproductive choice, and protecting voting rights in litigation against the federal government.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney; served as a state senator before being elected attorney general in 2018.

candidates.name: Bob Fioretti
candidates.runningOn: His campaign emphasizes civil rights, education, and public safety, with an overall message of integrity and independence in the attorney general's office. He presents himself as an alternative to continued Democratic control of the office.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney with decades of litigation experience; served as Chicago alderman for the 2nd Ward from 2007 to 2015.

candidates.name: Alexi Giannoulias
candidates.runningOn: Running for a second term on his record of modernizing the office, including the Skip the Line DMV appointment system, DMV kiosks in grocery stores, and a mobile DMV unit. He also cites legislation he backed against book banning in libraries, limits on using license plate data to track women seeking abortions across state lines, and easing license renewal requirements for older drivers.
candidates.priorCareer: Illinois state treasurer from 2007 to 2011, the youngest person elected to that office; secretary of state since 2023.

candidates.name: Diane Harris
candidates.runningOn: Says she is running to improve customer service at the secretary of state's office and build a faster, fairer experience for residents. She cites her experience with budgets, management, and customer relations from her corporate and elected roles.
candidates.priorCareer: Retired ComEd liability representative and small business owner from Joliet; serves as a Joliet Junior College trustee.

candidates.name: Margaret Croke
candidates.runningOn: Won a four-way Democratic primary for the seat being vacated by Susana Mendoza and is running on transparency, efficiency, and financial oversight. Her campaign message is to balance the state's books, pay bills on time, and pair fiscal responsibility with protecting vulnerable communities.
candidates.priorCareer: State representative for Chicago's 12th District since 2021.

candidates.name: Bryan Drew
candidates.runningOn: Running on affordability, accountability, and transparency. His campaign says he would work to stop government waste to lower costs for working families, increase transparency so taxpayers know where every dollar is spent, and act as a watchdog on how politicians spend tax money.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney and small business owner from Benton in southern Illinois.

candidates.name: Mike Frerichs
candidates.runningOn: Seeking a fourth term on his record as treasurer, including returning unclaimed property to residents, expanding the state's 529 college savings programs, and the ABLE savings program for people with disabilities.
candidates.priorCareer: Illinois state treasurer since 2015; previously a state senator from east-central Illinois.

candidates.name: Max Solomon
candidates.runningOn: Became the Republican nominee by receiving more than 5,000 write-in votes in the March primary after no Republican filed for the office. His campaign emphasizes faith-based public service, accessibility, and direct engagement with voters; he has not published a detailed policy platform for the office that we could find.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney, college political science instructor, and ordained minister from Hazel Crest.

candidates.name: Toni Preckwinkle
candidates.runningOn: Seeking a fifth term and says she wants to build on criminal justice reform, expanded health care access, and medical debt relief from her tenure. Her campaign points to balanced county budgets without new taxes and to preserving the county health system for all residents.
candidates.priorCareer: Cook County Board President since 2010 and the first Black woman elected to the role. She previously served nearly two decades as alderman of Chicago's 4th Ward.

candidates.name: Michael Murphy
candidates.runningOn: Calls for reducing property taxes to 1 percent based on purchase price, protecting personal liberty, safer communities through accountable governance, and more efficient delivery of county services, with a focus on transit reform, housing accessibility, and food security. He describes himself as an IT professional and problem solver rather than a career politician.
candidates.priorCareer: Information technology and systems management professional from Chicago's Austin neighborhood.

candidates.name: Pat Hynes
candidates.runningOn: Campaigns on making property assessments more accurate, equitable, and transparent, saying too many residents have found the system confusing and unfair. He emphasizes correcting the property tax rolls, including capturing new construction so existing homeowners do not absorb taxes that new properties should pay. He defeated two-term incumbent Fritz Kaegi in the March primary.
candidates.priorCareer: Lyons Township Assessor since 2021 with about 30 years in the property tax field, including 20 years as an appraiser in the Cook County Assessor's Office.

candidates.name: Nico Tsatsoulis
candidates.runningOn: Proposes limiting effective property taxes to 1 percent of a property's real value and basing assessments on actual sales prices rather than government estimates. He argues the current system disproportionately burdens middle-class and minority homeowners, and he also supports term limits and reducing the influence of money in politics.
candidates.priorCareer: Holds a BA and MBA from the University of Chicago; previously ran for Cook County Assessor in 2022 and the Board of Review in 2024.

candidates.name: Maria Pappas
candidates.runningOn: Runs on financial transparency and modernization of the treasurer's office, highlighting her Debt Disclosure Ordinance requiring local governments to report their debt and spending, and on technology that makes property tax information accessible online.
candidates.priorCareer: Cook County Treasurer since 1998; previously served on the Cook County Board of Commissioners.

candidates.name: Thomas Dart
candidates.runningOn: Seeking a sixth term, campaigning on public safety and community trust in government. His record includes programs aimed at reducing violence and connecting law enforcement with the communities it serves, such as the Sheriff's Anti-Violence Effort, which provides therapy and life-skills training for incarcerated young men.
candidates.priorCareer: Cook County Sheriff since 2006; previously an Illinois state legislator.

candidates.name: Brad Sandefur
candidates.runningOn: Campaigns on building a safer Cook County through fair justice and community collaboration. His stated priorities include reforming the SAFE-T Act with stronger public safety measures, expanding mental health and addiction treatment diversion programs, enhancing deputy training, and clearer disciplinary procedures with due process protections.
candidates.priorCareer: Cook County Sheriff's office employee since 1990 with 17 years as a shift commander; served in the US Marine Corps.

candidates.name: Monica Gordon
candidates.runningOn: Won a 2024 special election after the death of Clerk Karen Yarbrough and is seeking a full term. Her office oversees suburban Cook County elections, property tax extension, and countywide vital records. Her public messaging has emphasized election administration; no detailed 2026 campaign platform site was findable as of early September 2026.
candidates.priorCareer: Cook County Clerk since December 2024; previously a Cook County Commissioner.

candidates.name: Precious Brady-Davis
candidates.runningOn: Says she focuses on clean water, flood prevention, climate resilience, and strong public oversight, describing her approach as asking hard questions and studying the facts so decisions protect current and future generations.
candidates.priorCareer: Appointed to the MWRD board in 2023 and elected in 2024; previously associate regional communications director at the Sierra Club.

candidates.name: Eira Corral Sepulveda
candidates.runningOn: Describes the MWRD as sitting at the intersection of fighting climate change, infrastructure investment, workforce development, and equity, and is seeking a second 6-year term.
candidates.priorCareer: First Latina elected to the MWRD board, inaugurated in 2020; previously served three terms as Village Clerk of Hanover Park.

candidates.name: Beth McElroy Kirkwood
candidates.runningOn: Emphasizes safeguarding Lake Michigan and area waterways as climate change increases flooding risk and strains aging infrastructure. She is seeking a full 6-year term after being appointed to a vacant seat.
candidates.priorCareer: Appointed to the MWRD board in December 2024; Orland Township Democratic committeeperson and chair of the Moraine Valley Community College board of trustees.

candidates.name: Michelle Pennington
candidates.runningOn: Says the MWRD must balance environmental protection with fiscal responsibility, stating that the district must ensure that not a penny of taxpayer money is wasted.
candidates.priorCareer: Managing director of Medill Partners, a real estate development firm, with nonprofit work supporting Chicago Public Schools.

candidates.name: Timothy Rueckert
candidates.runningOn: Campaigns on flood mitigation and intergovernmental coordination, saying he would work with local, state, and federal governments to protect residents and water quality. He points to flood-control work during his time as a township highway commissioner.
candidates.priorCareer: Served eight years as Northfield Township highway commissioner; previously worked in state law enforcement roles and owns a small business.

candidates.name: Jill Shestokas
candidates.runningOn: Campaigns on public transparency about the MWRD's operations and funding, noting that most residents engage with the district only when heavy rains threaten their homes. She draws on her past work inside the district in policy and public education.
candidates.priorCareer: Former MWRD public affairs manager who worked on policy, legislative affairs, and public education.

candidates.name: Cameron Davis
candidates.runningOn: Running unopposed in a special election for a 2-year unexpired term, campaigning on four decades of clean water advocacy, including service as President Obama's Great Lakes coordinator and as president and CEO of the Alliance for the Great Lakes.
candidates.priorCareer: MWRD commissioner since 2018; coordinated Great Lakes restoration across 11 federal departments under the Obama administration EPA.
