candidates.seat: Vacancy of Hon. Mary L. Mikva
candidates.runningOn: Circuit judge appointed by the Illinois Supreme Court in 2025 after 37 years in the Cook County Public Defender's office, where he was chief of staff; won a three-way primary with 51.83%.

candidates.name: Jarrett Knox
candidates.seat: Vacancy of Hon. Pamela McLean Meyerson
candidates.runningOn: Cook County assistant state's attorney in the child protection division since 2019, formerly an attorney at the Cook County Public Guardian's office; won the primary over John R. Carrozza, 61.51% to 38.49%.

candidates.name: Kim Przekota
candidates.seat: Vacancy of Hon. Mary Colleen Roberts
candidates.runningOn: Circuit judge appointed by the Illinois Supreme Court in 2025, previously a Cook County assistant state's attorney (2008-2025); unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: Robert "Bob" Groebner
candidates.seat: Vacancy of Hon. John Curry, Jr.
candidates.runningOn: Cook County assistant state's attorney since 1999, currently assigned to the Skokie courthouse; unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: Brittany Michelle Pedersen
candidates.seat: Vacancy of Hon. Martin C. Kelley
candidates.runningOn: Managing partner of a Kane County criminal defense and civil litigation firm and a former Kane County assistant public defender who ran unsuccessfully for Kane County judge in 2020 and 2022; unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: William F. Kelley
candidates.seat: Vacancy of Hon. Thomas J. Kelley
candidates.runningOn: Managing partner of Kelley, Kelley & Kelley since 1984 and chair of the Harper College Board of Trustees; the seat was held by his brother Thomas J. Kelley, who retired in 2025; unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: Dan Naranjo
candidates.seat: Vacancy of Hon. Shannon P. O'Malley
candidates.runningOn: Circuit judge appointed by the Illinois Supreme Court in 2025 after 25 years as a Cook County assistant public defender; unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: Julian Sanchez Crozier
candidates.seat: Converted from Associate Judgeship of Hon. Callie L. Baird
candidates.runningOn: Criminal defense partner at a small firm (2018-2025) and a former Cook County assistant state's attorney (2013-2018); unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: Jessica Karina Velez
candidates.seat: Converted from Associate Judgeship of Hon. Patricia Mendoza
candidates.runningOn: Former deputy general counsel at the Illinois Office of the Comptroller (2023-2025) and civil litigation associate; unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: Natalia Moore
candidates.seat: Converted from Associate Judgeship of Hon. Lloyd J. Brooks
candidates.runningOn: Lead attorney in the Cook County State's Attorney's child support services division since 2008; won the primary over Meridth Hammer, 74.67% to 25.33%.

candidates.name: Bianca B. Brown
candidates.seat: Converted from Associate Judgeship of Hon. James R. Carroll
candidates.runningOn: Law firm associate, former chief attorney at the Chicago Transit Authority (2021-2025), and former Cook County assistant state's attorney and Illinois assistant attorney general; won a three-way primary with 57.81%.

candidates.name: Sam Bae
candidates.seat: Converted from Associate Judgeship of Hon. Frank J. Andreou
candidates.runningOn: Des Plaines attorney in private practice since 2012 and a former River Trails School District 26 board member; unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: Juan Ponce de Leon
candidates.seat: Converted from Associate Judgeship of Hon. Jeffrey G. Chrones
candidates.runningOn: Cook County assistant public defender since 2010, assigned to the Rolling Meadows courthouse; unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: Sara McGann
candidates.seat: Converted from Associate Judgeship of Hon. John A. Fairman
candidates.runningOn: Circuit judge appointed by the Illinois Supreme Court in July 2025, previously a Cook County assistant state's attorney supervising criminal appeals; unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: Monica Somerville
candidates.seat: Converted from Associate Judgeship of Hon. Michael J. Kane
candidates.runningOn: Staff attorney at Cabrini Green Legal Aid and a City of Chicago administrative hearing officer, formerly a deputy director in the Chicago Department of Finance; won a three-way primary with 42.39%.

candidates.name: Michael J. Zink
candidates.seat: Converted from Associate Judgeship of Hon. David E. Haracz
candidates.runningOn: Circuit judge appointed by the Illinois Supreme Court in 2024 after two decades as a partner in a housing and eviction law firm; unopposed in the primary.

candidates.name: Jon Stromsta
candidates.seat: Converted from Associate Judgeship of Hon. Stephanie K. Miller
candidates.runningOn: Administrative law judge at the Illinois Department of Employment Security since 2022 and a former assistant defender in the Office of the State Appellate Defender; won the primary over Belle Katubig, 58.16% to 41.84%.

candidates.name: Kam Buckner
candidates.runningOn: His own site does not publish an issues page for this race. Legislative focus areas reflected in his ilga.gov record include criminal justice reform, housing, health care access, election reform and economic development, and he serves as House Speaker Pro Tempore and chairs two tax policy subcommittees.
candidates.priorCareer: Was vice president of governmental affairs at Outfront Media, executive director of the youth nonprofit World Sport Chicago, a government relations manager for the Chicago Cubs, and an aide to U.S. Sen. Dick Durbin and New Orleans Mayor Mitch Landrieu; holds a J.D. from DePaul.

candidates.name: Justin Q. Slaughter
candidates.runningOn: His site lists criminal justice reform, education funding reform, small and minority business development, expanding health care and reducing health disparities, raising the minimum wage, and early childhood and child care access as his focus areas. He chairs the House Judiciary-Criminal Committee.
candidates.priorCareer: Worked as a policy advisor to Gov. Pat Quinn, deputy director at the Illinois Department of Juvenile Justice, legislative coordinator for the Cook County Bureau of Administration, and district director for Cook County Commissioner Stanley Moore and then-state Sen. Kwame Raoul.

candidates.name: Robert "Bob" Rita
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find. Wikipedia lists his stated priorities as economic redevelopment, equitable school funding and increased health care availability; on ilga.gov he is Deputy Majority Leader and chairs the General Services appropriations committee.
candidates.priorCareer: An operating engineer and member of IUOE Local 150 who has served in the House since 2003 and is also a Calumet Township Democratic committeeman and township trustee.

candidates.name: Thaddeus Jones
candidates.runningOn: His site highlights auto and property insurance affordability and consumer protections in insurance claims; he chairs the House Insurance Committee. His ilga.gov record also covers property taxes, health care access and economic development in Calumet City.
candidates.priorCareer: Serves as mayor of Calumet City, was the city's first Black alderman for its Third Ward, founded the Jones Foundation, and holds a criminal justice degree from Loyola University.

candidates.name: Michael "Mike" Crawford
candidates.runningOn: Says his priorities are increasing education funding and opportunities, equal rights, equitable health care access, supporting workers and their families, economic development, and public safety in the district. His site also cites work on students with disabilities, youth in care, and protecting seniors from scams.
candidates.priorCareer: A postsecondary educator and administrator who worked at The Chicago School, City Colleges of Chicago, Chicago State University and Northern Illinois University; holds a Ph.D. from Concordia University Chicago.

candidates.name: Lisa J. Davis
candidates.runningOn: Says she wants to be a voice for women, working families and seniors, keep communities safer, and make the criminal justice system fair. Her ilga.gov bill record covers maternal health education, school safety, substance abuse treatment and clean energy workforce development.
candidates.priorCareer: An attorney admitted to the Illinois bar in 2008 who works as an assistant public defender in the Cook County Public Defender's Office and is a member of AFSCME Local 3315.

candidates.name: Marcus C. Evans, Jr.
candidates.runningOn: His site lists energy reliability, labor rights and policy, transportation, health care funding and availability, and early childhood development as his issue areas. He is Assistant Majority Leader, chairs the House Labor and Commerce Committee, and became president of the National Conference of State Legislatures in August 2025.
candidates.priorCareer: Worked as deputy chief of staff for Chicago's 8th Ward alderman, is a licensed real estate appraiser and IHSA sports official, and has served in the House since 2012.

candidates.name: Cleopatra "Cleo" Cowley
candidates.runningOn: Says her top issue is community safety and that her approach is prevention-first, with investment in trauma-informed mental health services, violence interruption and youth and family support alongside accountability for offenders. Also lists economic development for small businesses and job training, equitable school funding, and access to affordable health care including trauma services. The seat is open because Rep. Nicholas Smith did not seek reelection.
candidates.priorCareer: A trained grief counselor and public speaker who became a gun violence prevention advocate after her daughter, Hadiya Pendleton, was killed in a 2013 shooting; she has partnered with the nonprofit Advocates of Change and holds a B.S. in computer science.

candidates.name: Miguel Alvelo-Rivera
candidates.runningOn: Says housing affordability is the district's most pressing problem and supports lifting the state ban on rent control, a graduated income tax on high earners and corporations to fund schools and health care, labor protections, climate resilience, and protections for immigrant, LGBTQ and disabled residents. He defeated incumbent Rep. Jaime Andrade Jr. in the March 17 Democratic primary with about 56 percent of the vote.
candidates.priorCareer: Executive director of the Latino Union of Chicago, a workers' rights organization, and a former adult literacy educator and after-school program director; holds a B.S. from Northland University and an M.A. from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee.

candidates.name: Lindsey LaPointe
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists reducing gun violence, support for first responders, health care and mental health, ethics reform, women's and LGBTQ rights, and the environment as her issues. In a 2024 Nadig Newspapers candidate profile she said she was leading a bill to grow behavioral health insurance networks by raising provider reimbursement rates and backed a two-year legislator-to-lobbyist ban.
candidates.priorCareer: Social worker who was a justice-reform project manager at Business and Professional People for the Public Interest and a program manager for Adult Redeploy Illinois at the Illinois Criminal Justice Information Authority; in the House since July 2019.

candidates.name: John "JZ" Zimmers
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site describes his platform as a four-legged stool of public school reform, public safety reform, tax reform and immigration reform, including reinstating trade programs in Chicago schools, backing law enforcement, and reducing the number of Illinois government units. In a 2024 Nadig Newspapers profile he called for repealing the SAFE-T Act and cited vacant Chicago police positions.
candidates.priorCareer: Residential real estate broker for the past twelve years who says he has worked in real estate as an asset and property manager, lender and broker throughout his adult life.

candidates.name: Brad Stephens
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find; he is unopposed. Bills he has sponsored, as listed on ilga.gov, cover transportation, property taxation, insurance regulation, public safety and municipal governance.
candidates.priorCareer: Mayor of Rosemont since 2007, previously a Rosemont village trustee (1989-2007) and Leyden Township supervisor, and a former member of the Illinois Tollway and Pace boards; in the House since June 2019, where he is an Assistant Minority Leader.

candidates.name: Abdelnasser Rashid
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site says he is focused on affordability, good-paying jobs, and protecting the community from what it calls Trump's attacks. His bio there says he is working to root out corruption, fund public education, and change a property tax system he describes as favoring large corporations over working families.
candidates.priorCareer: Held government and organizing roles in affordable housing and immigrant rights advocacy before his 2022 election; holds a Harvard B.A. and a University of Chicago Booth MBA.

candidates.name: Eric Su
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site names high property taxes, education quality and high health care costs as his three focus issues, and says he supports property tax relief, expanded access to affordable health care and mental health services, career and technical education, and fair wages that do not harm small businesses. He told the Riverside-Brookfield Landmark in 2025 he proposes a health savings match for low-income families and learn-and-earn labs linking high school students with employers.
candidates.priorCareer: Fitness trainer and small business owner for more than 20 years, a Purdue University graduate and former election judge who lives in North Riverside.

candidates.name: Angie Guerrero-Cuellar
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists safer neighborhoods (cutting carjackings, catalytic converter thefts and drag racing), protecting abortion rights and women's health services, vocational training and apprenticeships for higher-paying jobs, and access to parks and youth programs as her issues.
candidates.priorCareer: Former community outreach organizer for COVID-19 response on the Southwest Side and former auxiliary board member of the National Museum of Mexican Art; in the House since February 2021.

candidates.name: Edgar Gonzalez, Jr.
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find; he is unopposed. Bills he has sponsored, as listed on ilga.gov, cover technology regulation, gaming, workforce development, education, health care and consumer protection.
candidates.priorCareer: Former in-district constituent services staffer for U.S. Rep. García and a Harvard graduate in government and economics; in the House since January 2020, where he is an Assistant Majority Leader.

candidates.name: Theresa Mah
candidates.runningOn: Her website says she has focused on education, job growth and immigrant rights, and lists public education and bilingual programs, immigrant integration, health care access and consumer protection, language access, and support for seniors and small businesses as priorities during her tenure.
candidates.priorCareer: Former college professor with a University of Chicago Ph.D., community organizer, and senior policy advisor to Gov. Pat Quinn; in the House since January 2017.

candidates.name: Curtis J. Tarver II
candidates.runningOn: His website says his priorities are good jobs, better quality education, sound fiscal management and justice for all people in Illinois, and describes work on streamlining regulations for small business owners and changes to criminal law.
candidates.priorCareer: Trial attorney in personal injury and civil rights cases with a J.D. from the University of Iowa; in the House since January 2019, where he chairs the Revenue and Finance Committee.

candidates.name: Antoinette Jewel Simmons
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists education equity, expanding access to affordable health care, workforce development, modernizing law enforcement alongside community-based public safety, environmental protection, and investment in roads, bridges and transit. Its tagline calls for better schools, safer streets and fair wages.
candidates.priorCareer: Community organizer who has worked as a contractor at the South Side Community Art Center since 2015, was an executive assistant at the DuSable Museum (2001-2014), and was general manager of Urban Broadcast Media.

candidates.name: Aaron M. Ortiz
candidates.runningOn: No campaign site found. Recent legislation highlighted on his House Democratic caucus page includes restricting where immigration detention centers can be sited, expanding tuition assistance for community college students, requiring grocery chains that offer e-coupons to honor a paper alternative, and expanding insurance coverage for children's speech-language therapy.
candidates.priorCareer: Full-time legislator since January 2019 who previously worked as an educator and college counselor at Chicago Public Schools.

candidates.name: Eva-Dina Delgado
candidates.runningOn: No campaign site found. Recent items on her House Democratic caucus page focus on housing and child care affordability, public transit reform and safety, lowering student loan interest rates, and limiting immigration enforcement in sensitive locations.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney who worked as chief of staff and assistant to the president at Peoples Gas and served on the Chicago Police Board from 2016 to 2019 before being appointed to the House in November 2019.

candidates.name: Lilian Jimenez
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site says she wants to tax corporations and high earners rather than working people, stabilize property taxes, expand community land trusts, protect reproductive rights, and restrict immigration enforcement at schools, courthouses, day cares, universities, and hospitals. In a Sun-Times questionnaire she named ICE enforcement, health care, housing, child care costs, and property taxes as the district's top concerns.
candidates.priorCareer: Immigration and labor attorney who served as chief of staff to Cook County Commissioner Jesus 'Chuy' Garcia, director of the Fair Labor Standards Division at the Illinois Department of Labor, and administrator of the Office of Welcoming Centers at the Illinois Department of Human Services.

candidates.name: Kimberly Neely DuBuclet
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists public safety, public education, government accountability, health care, reproductive health care, and economic development as her issues. She says her mission is growing opportunities for the South Side, including environmental justice, clean air and water, and sustainable economic development.
candidates.priorCareer: Former vice president of the Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago board, former legislative and community affairs director for the Chicago Park District, and former adjunct professor at Roosevelt University; in the House since May 2023.

candidates.name: Sonya Marie Harper
candidates.runningOn: No campaign site found. Issue areas listed on her legislative office site include agriculture and cannabis, economic opportunity and equity, food access, public safety and violence reduction, education, health care and human services, people with records, and the environment; it highlights her work on cannabis social equity provisions and the Illinois Farmer Equity Act.
candidates.priorCareer: Executive director of Grow Greater Englewood and president of Sharper PR Communications, a former television news producer, and a former outreach director at Growing Home Inc.; in the House since October 2015.

candidates.name: Shantel Franklin
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists housing stability, stronger schools, health care access and affordability, economic development, and a public safety approach combining prevention, protection, and opportunity. After winning the March primary she told Austin Weekly News that affordability and the cost of living are her top concerns and that she hopes to serve on the housing, appropriations, and education committees.
candidates.priorCareer: Real estate agent who spent six years as a community outreach and legislative liaison aide in the office of Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul.

candidates.name: Yolonda Morris
candidates.runningOn: No campaign site found. Her ilga.gov biography says she has advocated for the Fight for 15 minimum wage campaign, safe staffing, and child care for all; her office site lists committee work on public safety appropriations, health care access, housing, human services, mental health and addiction, and public health.
candidates.priorCareer: Certified nursing assistant for 26 years and a former SEIU union organizer; appointed to the House in September 2023.

candidates.name: Jawaharial "Omar" Williams
candidates.runningOn: No campaign site found. His House Democratic caucus page describes his focus as improving access to health care, safer communities, and increasing economic prosperity; he chairs the House Prescription Drug Affordability Committee and has sponsored legislation expanding access to opioid overdose antagonists at concert venues.
candidates.priorCareer: Former laborer with the Chicago Department of Water Management and member of the Laborers' International Union and Plumbers Local 130, and former president of the Young Democrats of Illinois; appointed to the House in May 2019.

candidates.name: Ann M. Williams
candidates.runningOn: No campaign site found. Her office site says her legislative work has centered on environment, sustainability and clean energy policy, supporting neighborhood schools, protecting human services, preventing gun violence, state fiscal stability, reproductive rights, and data privacy; she chairs the House Executive Committee.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney who served as an assistant attorney general and legislative director under Illinois Attorney General Lisa Madigan; in the House since January 2011.

candidates.name: Omar Aquino
candidates.runningOn: Legislative focus areas listed in his ilga.gov biography are improving education, aging services and human services. He chairs the Senate's Appropriations - Health and Human Services and Government Operations committees and serves as Majority Caucus Chair.
candidates.priorCareer: Worked as a bilingual case manager for low-income seniors in the state's Community Care Program, as a legislative aide in the Illinois House, and as outreach coordinator for Congresswoman Tammy Duckworth before joining the Senate in 2016.

candidates.name: Mattie Hunter
candidates.runningOn: Recent announcements on her legislative office site emphasize health care access and mental health coverage transparency, library and adult literacy funding, affordable housing, and removing certain chemicals from beauty products. On ilga.gov she is listed as co-chair of task forces on missing and murdered Chicago women, kidney disease prevention and Medicaid managed care oversight.
candidates.priorCareer: A full-time state legislator since 2003 and Assistant Majority Leader, she is a certified drug and alcohol counselor and prevention specialist with a sociology master's degree from Jackson State University.

candidates.name: Lakesia Collins
candidates.runningOn: Her ilga.gov biography lists seniors, working-class families, youth in care, education, public safety, affordable housing and mental health as her focus areas, and says she works toward development without displacement in the 5th District.
candidates.priorCareer: Worked as a certified nursing assistant in nursing homes and as a labor organizer and Fight for 15 spokesperson, then served in the Illinois House from 2020 to 2023, where she chaired the House Black Caucus.

candidates.name: Sara Feigenholtz
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists education access, public safety including an assault weapons ban, health care and senior care, abortion access and LGBTQ rights, and renewable energy and climate as her priorities. She won the March 2026 Democratic primary over Nick Uniejewski with about 56 percent of the vote.
candidates.priorCareer: A full-time legislator, she served in the Illinois House from 1995 to 2020 before being appointed to the Senate seat in 2020.

candidates.name: Mike Porfirio
candidates.runningOn: Bills he has sponsored, as listed on ilga.gov, center on veterans' affairs and procurement preferences for veteran-owned businesses, first responder support, transportation, local government operations and property taxes. We could not find a published 2026 campaign platform.
candidates.priorCareer: A Naval Academy graduate and Navy Reserve officer who served in Iraq and Afghanistan, he was administrator of the Village of Summit, public works director in Bridgeview and a Lyons Township trustee before his 2022 election to the Senate.

candidates.name: Celina Villanueva
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site describes her as a former organizer and labor leader focused on health care access, working families and labor issues. On ilga.gov she chairs the Senate Revenue Committee, and her sponsored bills cover tax policy, immigrant protections, environmental justice and workers' rights.
candidates.priorCareer: A full-time legislator raised in Little Village, she was civic and youth engagement manager at the Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights and served in the Illinois House from 2019 to 2020 before joining the Senate.

candidates.name: Napoleon B. Harris III
candidates.runningOn: Recent announcements on his legislative office site focus on workforce training through the Workforce Pell program, library grants, funding for fire protection districts and neighborhood infrastructure in the 15th District. On ilga.gov he chairs the Senate Firearms Committee and serves as Assistant Majority Leader.
candidates.priorCareer: A former NFL linebacker and Northwestern University graduate, he is an entrepreneur and has served in the Senate since 2013.

candidates.name: Graciela Guzman
candidates.runningOn: In a 2024 Sun-Times candidate questionnaire she said her priorities were expanding health coverage and affordable prescriptions, addressing housing and health costs, tightening ethics and campaign finance rules, and funding pensions through progressive taxation. Bills she has sponsored, as listed on ilga.gov, cover health care access, housing affordability, labor protections and immigrant rights.
candidates.priorCareer: A health care and education organizer with the Healthy Illinois campaign, Protect Our Care Illinois and the Chicago Teachers Union, she also served as chief of staff to State Sen. Cristina Pacione-Zayas before taking office in 2025.

candidates.name: Don Harmon
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site lists criminal justice reform and police accountability, LGBTQ equality and voting rights, a balanced budget with tax relief, increased school and early childhood funding, ethics and campaign finance reform, and gun safety measures such as universal background checks as his priorities.
candidates.priorCareer: An attorney with a J.D. and M.B.A. from the University of Chicago, he has represented Oak Park in the Senate since 2003 and has served as Senate President since January 2020.

candidates.name: Niki Conforti
candidates.runningOn: Conforti says affordability is the district's most critical issue and lists cutting energy regulations, increasing transparency in medical billing, and bringing manufacturing back to the district through workforce training as her three priorities. Her campaign site lists opposition to raising the debt ceiling, support for tariffs, expanding ICE and deporting violent criminals, stronger penalties for fentanyl crimes, and a photo ID requirement to vote. She describes herself as pro-life with exceptions for rape, incest, and the life of the mother, and supports term limits for House members.
candidates.priorCareer: Energy consultant since 2017 with earlier work as a director in the health care industry, and the 2024 Republican nominee for this seat.

candidates.name: Sean Casten
candidates.runningOn: Casten's campaign site says he is running on lowering costs, creating jobs, affirming women's rights, protecting seniors, and advocating for clean energy. On energy and climate he lists eliminating fossil fuel tax subsidies, expanding grid transmission, and requiring corporate climate risk disclosure, and points to his role in the Inflation Reduction Act. On health care he says he wants to make ACA premium tax credits permanent, expand Medicare drug price negotiation, and penalize drug price gouging.
candidates.priorCareer: Scientist and clean energy executive who was president and CEO of Turbosteam Corporation and co-founded Recycled Energy Development before his election to Congress in 2018.

candidates.name: Chad Koppie
candidates.runningOn: Koppie's campaign site summarizes his platform as "Life, Liberty, Limited Government" and says the principle of limited government is vital to restoring America. His issues page says the national debt and deficit prevent economic growth, that the federal government has no constitutional authority over public education, and that the traditional family unit must be restored. He also lists free-market health care, control over immigration as a matter of sovereignty, and abolishing the Federal Reserve and the IRS.
candidates.priorCareer: Retired Delta Airlines jumbo jet captain and lifelong farmer who serves on the Kane County Regional Board of Schools and previously was a township trustee and local school board member.

candidates.name: La Shawn K. Ford
candidates.runningOn: Ford's campaign site lists health care that puts people first, living wages for today's cost of living, child care and early learning, an affordable housing plan for the 7th District, and support for troops and veterans as his platform planks, and contrasts a "Project 2027" with Project 2025. His about page says his priorities include jobs and economic mobility through small business support, mental health and opioid crisis response, record sealing, expungement, and bail reform, and protection from foreclosure and eviction. He campaigns on 19 years in the Illinois House as experience that is ready on day one.
candidates.priorCareer: Chicago Public Schools teacher and coach who later opened a real estate business, and a member of the Illinois House of Representatives for the 8th district since 2007.

candidates.name: Angel Oakley
candidates.runningOn: Oakley's campaign policy page lists ten areas, including government accountability and transparency, election reform with national voter ID standards, cutting federal spending and small-business regulation, border security, and defending constitutional rights including free speech and the Second Amendment. She also lists balanced budgets, a prevention and patient-choice approach to healthcare she calls medical freedom, and privacy and accountability rules for AI and technology. Her BallotReady profile summarizes her positions as ending the surveillance state, cutting inflation and housing costs, shrinking the deficit, addressing chronic disease, and securing the border with immigration reform.
candidates.priorCareer: BallotReady lists her work as a cannabis educator, advisor, and CBD broker since 2017 and in Airbnb hospitality and property management since 2023, with bachelor's and master's degrees from Judson University.

candidates.name: Delia Ramirez
candidates.runningOn: Ramirez's campaign site says she is running on housing justice, healthcare for all, public education, community safety, community-centered economic development, and the rights of women and the LGBTQ+ community. Her issue pages say she supports Medicare for All and legislation to lower prescription drug costs, building affordable housing and protecting renters from corporate landlords, and a pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants including permanent status for DACA recipients. She also lists co-leading the Dream and Promise Act and pushing comprehensive immigration reform.
candidates.priorCareer: She served in the Illinois House of Representatives for the 4th District from 2018 to 2023, where she was Majority Floor Leader, after 18 years in nonprofit leadership including chairing the boards of LUCHA and the Logan Square Neighborhood Association.

candidates.name: Tommy Hanson
candidates.runningOn: Hanson's campaign issues page lists the family, the economy, growth and development, crime, immigration, small business, and inflation. He says he is pro-life, wants to use the Tenth Amendment to limit federal spending, supports prosecuting violent criminals without early release and fully supporting law enforcement, backs lawful immigration while opposing illegal immigration and open borders, and says inflation is a government-created problem that Congress must address by not printing money. In a 2024 Sun-Times questionnaire he named crime, the economy, and mental health as his top issues.
candidates.priorCareer: He is a commercial real estate broker who earlier sold advertising for the Chicago Tribune and U.S. News & World Report, and has been the Republican nominee against Quigley in several prior cycles.

candidates.name: Mike Quigley
candidates.runningOn: In his 2026 Sun-Times questionnaire, Quigley says the most important issue facing his constituents is the affordability crisis, and that he will keep prioritizing federal funding for transportation infrastructure and housing through his seat on the Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing, and Urban Development. He also lists transparency and accountability, defending the LGBTQ+ community, environmental protection, and bipartisan problem-solving. His campaign site issues page adds mandatory background checks on all gun sales, comprehensive immigration reform, opposition to privatizing Medicare, and a diplomacy-first foreign policy.
candidates.priorCareer: He served on the Cook County Board of Commissioners from 1998 to 2009 and taught environmental policy and Chicago politics as an adjunct professor at Loyola University Chicago.

candidates.name: Christian Maxwell
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists public safety, economic growth, education reform, and family policy as her platform, including support for law enforcement, tax relief, school choice, and maternal care and childcare access. In her Chicago Sun-Times questionnaire she says her priorities are improving children's literacy through school choice, addressing property crime, reducing taxes, and requiring accountability for how federal dollars are spent.
candidates.priorCareer: E-commerce growth marketing consultant and marketing strategist with no prior elected office.

candidates.name: Jonathan L. Jackson
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site lists economic justice and reducing wealth inequality, criminal justice reform and police accountability, free community college and student debt relief, Medicare for All, a transition to renewable energy, fresh food access in underserved communities, and gun violence prevention as his priorities. His House site says he serves on the Agriculture and Foreign Affairs committees and emphasizes constituent services.
candidates.priorCareer: Before Congress he worked in finance and business, taught at Chicago State University and City Colleges of Chicago, and served as national spokesman for the Rainbow/PUSH Coalition; he has represented Illinois's 1st district since January 2023.

candidates.name: Michael Scott Noack
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site's issues page says he wants to convert health insurance companies to nonprofit organizations, invest in hydroelectric power, focus immigration enforcement on violent criminals while fixing the legal immigration process, cut taxes and federal spending, and support veterans. In news coverage he cites grocery prices, gas prices, the state gas tax, and overall affordability as his reasons for running.
candidates.priorCareer: Truck driver from Bonfield in Kankakee County who has not previously run for office.

candidates.name: Donna Miller
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign's priorities page lists healthcare under a Medicare for All framework, lowering prescription drug costs and capping insulin prices, maternal health and reproductive rights, jobs and lower costs, climate, a path to citizenship with due process protections, gun laws and violence prevention, voting rights, veterans, and protecting Social Security. In her Chicago Sun-Times questionnaire she says health care is the major thread running through her district's issues and that she would work to restore Affordable Care Act tax credits.
candidates.priorCareer: Cook County Commissioner for the 6th district since 2018, previously a healthcare and pharmaceutical industry consultant and account specialist and board chair of Planned Parenthood Illinois.

candidates.name: Jennifer Davis
candidates.runningOn: Davis's campaign site lists small business, education, immigration, national security, community safety and tax relief as her issues, and says she wants to cut taxes, streamline regulations and expand school options including public, charter, private and home schools. She says she supports securing the border with technology, enforcing existing immigration law and prioritizing legal immigration, and proposes a national cyber defense she calls a Digital Dome. In her Sun-Times questionnaire she names affordability as the district's most important issue and says she backs term limits and independent redistricting commissions.
candidates.priorCareer: Co-founded the field service software company Davisware with her husband and later founded BExponential, an organization for women entrepreneurs; she has not held elected office.

candidates.name: Melissa L. Bean
candidates.runningOn: Bean's campaign site says she is running to restore democracy, health care and the economy, and lists lowering housing, health care, energy and education costs as priorities. She says she will protect and strengthen the Affordable Care Act, support comprehensive immigration reform with a pathway to citizenship, protect the right to organize, expand access to capital for small businesses and work to restore the U.S. Department of Education. Her issues page also lists codifying Roe v. Wade protections, campaign finance transparency, election security legislation and clean energy investment.
candidates.priorCareer: Represented Illinois's 8th District in the U.S. House from 2005 to 2011, then led the Executives Club of Chicago, chaired JPMorgan Chase's Midwest operations and served as CEO of Mesirow Wealth Advisors.

candidates.name: John Elleson
candidates.runningOn: Elleson describes himself as a compassionate conservative and organizes his campaign around building trust, empowering families and bridging communities. His stances page says he favors aid-based programs for addiction, homelessness and mental health, removing regulations he calls burdensome to support small business, supporting law enforcement alongside de-escalation and community trust, and community-first health care with more local clinics. In his Sun-Times questionnaire he says he would restore pro-growth tax and regulatory policies and pursue energy independence, and names affordability and the cost of living as the district's top local issue.
candidates.priorCareer: Pastor of Lakewood Chapel in Arlington Heights with about 40 years in Chicago-area ministry, and the 2018 Republican nominee for this seat.

candidates.name: Daniel Biss
candidates.runningOn: Biss's campaign site says his priorities are protecting communities, lowering costs and building a government that works for everyone, and his issues page lists restoring antitrust enforcement, strengthening workers' right to organize, climate action, campaign finance reform and lowering housing, health care and child care costs. In his Sun-Times questionnaire he says he supports a national single-payer system such as Medicare for All, says ICE should be abolished, and backs a path to citizenship and a ban on stock trading by members of Congress. He also lists gun violence reduction, public school investment and protecting Social Security and Medicare.
candidates.priorCareer: Mayor of Evanston since 2021; previously served in the Illinois House and the Illinois Senate.

candidates.name: Lupe Castillo
candidates.runningOn: Castillo's campaign site lists no tax on tips and overtime, voter ID for voting and registration, border security, school choice for low-income families, and support for law enforcement. She also says she wants to protect women's sports and girls' bathrooms, direct federal funds to needy Americans rather than nonprofits, and end congressional pay during government shutdowns. In an April 2026 Chicago Tribune interview she said businesses in the district need more support and that immigrants should come to the country legally.
candidates.priorCareer: A Little Village resident of more than four decades, she is a former pharmacy technician who previously served as 22nd Ward Republican committeewoman and was the district's Republican nominee in 2024.

candidates.name: Patty Garcia
candidates.runningOn: Garcia's campaign site lists raising the federal minimum wage, passing the PRO Act, expanding the Child Tax Credit, Medicare for All, and fully funding public schools. She says she supports a pathway to citizenship, protections for Dreamers and mixed-status families, and restructuring immigration agencies including abolishing ICE, along with reversing Citizens United, a ban on congressional stock trading, clean energy investment, and an immediate and permanent ceasefire in Gaza. In a July 2026 Sun-Times interview she said voters are raising immigration enforcement, the cost of rent and medicine, and reproductive rights.
candidates.priorCareer: She served as district director and then chief of staff to Rep. Jesus 'Chuy' Garcia (no relation) for more than seven years and holds a PhD in education policy from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

candidates.name: Ed Hershey
candidates.runningOn: At an April 2026 candidate forum at UIC, Hershey said he is running against the system, criticized both major parties for deporting immigrants and spending heavily on wars, and called for abolishing ICE. In his 2024 Sun-Times questionnaire for this seat he called for automatic wage increases tied to inflation, a shorter work week at full pay, full rights for all immigrants, and an end to U.S. military aid to Israel. He says the goal of his campaign is to build a party that the working class can organize around its own needs.
candidates.priorCareer: He has taught at Lindblom High School on Chicago's South Side for more than 16 years, served as a union representative in his school, and was the Working Class Party nominee for this district in 2022 and 2024.

candidates.name: Chris Getty
candidates.runningOn: Getty's campaign site lists cost of living, immigration and public safety, and government accountability as his priorities, and says he wants to restore trust in government and protect the integrity of elections. At an April 2026 UIC forum he said he does not support abolishing ICE, that there should be a clear process for immigrants to become citizens, and that federal agents should not come into neighborhoods to detain people. In August 2026 he told Desplaines Valley News that the cost of living was the top issue he heard while gathering petition signatures.
candidates.priorCareer: He has been mayor of Lyons, Illinois since 2009, also serves as Lyons Township supervisor, and works as a licensed insurance producer.

candidates.name: Tara Stamps
candidates.runningOn: Stamps has said her first priorities on the board are housing and safety. She supports countywide programs to address housing insecurity and homelessness, funded in part by asking wealthier property owners to pay more, and wants to expand programming for incarcerated youth.
candidates.priorCareer: Former Chicago Public Schools teacher who administered the Chicago Teachers Union's New Teacher Development program before her 2023 appointment to the board.

candidates.name: Michael Scott, Jr.
candidates.runningOn: Scott says his priorities are expanding access to affordable housing and health care. His district office site lists public safety, economic growth, and quality-of-life improvements for residents as his focus areas.
candidates.priorCareer: Alderman of Chicago's 24th Ward from 2015 to 2022, then head of industry and community relations at Cinespace Chicago Film Studios; earlier worked for the Chicago Park District, Chicago Public Schools, and After School Matters.

candidates.name: Bill Lowry
candidates.runningOn: Lowry's campaign site organizes his platform around health equity, economic equity, community equity, and environmental equity. It cites restoring ambulance service at Provident Hospital, a free birthday cancer-screening program, easing medical debt, access to capital for minority- and women-owned businesses, and his advocacy for the state assault weapons ban.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney specializing in employer liability and workers' compensation law, president of the firm Nyhan, Bambrick, Kinzie & Lowry, and a former member of the Illinois Capital Development Board.

candidates.name: Stanley S. Moore
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.
candidates.priorCareer: Former legislative budget analyst for Illinois Senate President Emil Jones Jr., project director in the Cook County Office of Capital Planning and Policy, and a director at the Illinois Department of Transportation.

candidates.name: George A. Cardenas
candidates.runningOn: Cardenas says his focus is fairness for every property owner through fair appeals, transparent policy, and direct constituent services. His listed initiatives include a property tax transparency dashboard with township-level and class-level trends, advocacy for circuit breaker relief for income-constrained homeowners, appeal-readiness workshops so residents file complete appeals on time, a single process map linking the Assessor, Board of Review, Treasurer, and Clerk, and a planned small business and commercial equity review.
candidates.priorCareer: Cardenas served 20 years as Chicago's 12th Ward alderman, is a U.S. Navy veteran, and worked for Fortune 500 companies before entering government.

candidates.name: Elizabeth "Liz" Nicholson
candidates.runningOn: Nicholson says every property owner or renter deserves a property tax system that is fair, transparent, and predictable, and that every taxpayer appealing an assessment should get a fair chance to reduce their bill. Her stated priorities are making appeals more accessible to working families and small businesses rather than those who hire connected attorneys, modernizing the process with clearer online tools and multilingual support, publishing more appeals data to identify systemic inequities, community outreach through neighborhood groups, schools, and libraries, and stricter ethics rules to limit the influence of property tax lawyers and special interests.
candidates.priorCareer: Nicholson was a longtime campaign adviser to former Illinois Senate President John Cullerton and held state posts including top aide to Secretary of State Jesse White, deputy director of the Illinois Department of Employment Security, and chief operating officer of Central Management Services.

candidates.name: Vince Romano
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.
candidates.priorCareer: Has worked in real estate and finance, as a self-defense instructor and small business owner, and was the Republican nominee for Illinois House District 16 in 2012 and 2022.

candidates.name: Ram Villivalam
candidates.runningOn: His official biography says his focus is income inequality, reducing gun violence, quality education regardless of zip code, and advancing immigrant, LGBTQ, and women's rights. He has held the seat since 2019 and serves as Senate Majority Caucus Whip.
candidates.priorCareer: Former legislative coordinator for SEIU Healthcare, outreach director for U.S. Rep. Brad Schneider, and past president of the Indo-American Democratic Organization.

candidates.name: Tom Lally
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.

candidates.name: Patrick Hanley
candidates.runningOn: His campaign is organized around the themes safe, green, and growing: lowering healthcare and housing costs, community and school safety, clean energy and job creation, and ethics reforms including an independent ethics commission and real-time campaign finance disclosure. He is running for the open seat being vacated by Laura Fine.
candidates.priorCareer: Small business owner (co-owner of a linen bedding company), president of the New Trier Democrats, and chair of a local Environmental and Forestry Commission.

candidates.name: Brian Skala
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site lists lower taxes, lower utility bills, and safer communities as its key issues, along with job creation and keeping families in Illinois.
candidates.priorCareer: Plumbers Local 130 member since 1997 and an elected Village of Crestwood trustee who previously served on the Crestwood Planning and Zoning Committee.

candidates.name: Emil Jones, III
candidates.runningOn: His official site lists bringing more jobs to the 14th District, a responsible solution to the state budget, and ending business as usual in Springfield as his top priorities, with current legislative work on education funding, healthcare access, public transit, and food security. He has held the seat since 2009.
candidates.priorCareer: Former administrator at the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity; son of former Senate President Emil Jones Jr.

candidates.name: Justin J. Kumar
candidates.runningOn: Lists fiscal responsibility, including a full review of the state budget, public safety, infrastructure, and lowering costs for food, medicine, transportation, education, and property taxes as his priorities. Says he would emphasize bipartisan collaboration and practical problem-solving.
candidates.priorCareer: President and CEO of Frontload Group LLC, an investment holding company, with a background in private equity and venture capital, and a board member of the Lupus Society of Illinois.

candidates.name: Paul Kendrick
candidates.runningOn: Campaigns on public safety, lower costs, and stronger communities, citing property tax relief through expanded homestead exemptions, housing and childcare costs, violence intervention and police recruitment, and ethics reforms such as limits on legislators' outside employment. Also lists reproductive rights, education funding, and environmental protection.
candidates.priorCareer: Nonprofit leader and author who worked in the Obama administration's Department of Education and White House, at Harlem Children's Zone, Hope Chicago, and Rust Belt Rising, and served on the Lincoln Park High School Local School Council.

candidates.name: Terry Nguyen Le
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.
candidates.priorCareer: Home caregiver and University of Illinois Chicago graduate who was the Republican candidate for this same seat in 2024.

candidates.name: Demerike "Demi" Palecek
candidates.runningOn: Lists affordable housing (rent stabilization, tenant protections, SRO preservation), healthcare and mental health access, reproductive freedom, public school funding including universal pre-K, union rights and fair wages, and climate investment as priorities. Supports a graduated income tax and ethics reforms such as barring legislators from outside lobbying work.
candidates.priorCareer: Marketing and communications consultant and Army National Guard member (previously U.S. Air Force Security Forces), former communications manager for state Rep. Stephanie Kifowit, and president of the 46th Ward Democrats.

candidates.name: Kelly M. Cassidy
candidates.runningOn: Her office site lists criminal justice reform, equality and LGBTQ+ rights, reproductive rights, healthcare access, affordable housing, and support for working families as her focus areas, along with constituent services through the district office.
candidates.priorCareer: State representative since 2011; previously legislative director for the National Organization for Women's Chicago office, an aide to state Sen. John Cullerton, and a programs and grants official in the Cook County State's Attorney's Office.

candidates.name: Michael J. Kelly
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site lists gun violence prevention, lowering healthcare costs including insurance premiums and prescription drugs, equal pay, affordable childcare and paid family leave, school and mental health funding, and support for first responders as priorities.
candidates.priorCareer: Chicago Fire Department firefighter and Local 2 union member for about 20 years, and a former coach and athletic director at Saint Edward Elementary School; chairs the House Police and Fire Committee.

candidates.name: Kevin John Olickal
candidates.runningOn: Says his focus is working-class families, constituent services, civic engagement, and inclusive legislation for what his office describes as the most diverse House district in Illinois.
candidates.priorCareer: Formerly on House Democratic staff, executive director of the Indo-American Democratic Organization, and a Cook County COVID-19 recovery specialist for small businesses; a lifelong Skokie resident serving in the House since 2023.

candidates.name: Pete Donaghue
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.

candidates.name: Robyn Gabel
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists a fiscally and socially responsible state budget, expanding affordability, access to quality health care, comprehensive clean energy policy, and protecting vulnerable residents as priorities.
candidates.priorCareer: Executive director of EverThrive Illinois, a nonprofit health advocacy organization, from 1988 to 2010; in the House since 2010 and House Majority Leader since 2023.

candidates.name: Cesar A. Guillen
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.

candidates.name: Will Guzzardi
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site lists public school funding, good-paying jobs, guaranteed health care access, criminal justice reform, protections for immigrants, LGBT rights, and clean energy. In a 2024 Sun-Times questionnaire he named affordable housing as the district's most pressing problem and supported a state tax credit for new housing units.
candidates.priorCareer: Former journalist at Huffington Post Chicago and head writer for the University of Chicago admissions office; in the House since 2015 and currently Assistant Majority Leader.

candidates.name: Joseph Johnson
candidates.runningOn: His campaign lists cutting taxes and lowering costs, supporting small businesses and job growth, protecting parental rights in education, and backing law enforcement to create safe communities.
candidates.priorCareer: Worked in finance for 14 years before starting a consulting business; a DePaul University graduate and first-time candidate from Glenview.

candidates.name: Justin Cochran
candidates.runningOn: Has said funding mass transit is a key issue for the district; his office site highlights workforce development, consumer product ingredient labeling, and updating disability terminology in state law.
candidates.priorCareer: Archivist with the Illinois State Archives, then chief of staff to State Rep. Marty Moylan from 2019 until his appointment to the seat on December 30, 2025.

candidates.name: Julian-Jahleel Randolph Jemison
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.

candidates.name: Camille Lilly
candidates.runningOn: Her district site lists health equity, strong schools, safe neighborhoods, economic opportunity, affordable health care access, school funding, and arts and cultural enhancement as focus areas.
candidates.priorCareer: Former vice president for external affairs and development at Loretto Hospital and executive director of the Austin Chamber of Commerce; in the House since 2010 and currently Assistant Majority Leader.

candidates.name: Frederick L. Walls
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.
candidates.priorCareer: Carpenter and entrepreneur from Crete who was the Republican nominee for the 34th Illinois House District in 2024.

candidates.name: Elgie R. Sims, Jr.
candidates.runningOn: As Senate Majority Caucus Appropriations Leader he describes his budget priorities as educating young people, expanding good-paying job opportunities, and keeping communities safe; his recent legislative work has focused on criminal justice measures such as the Clean Slate Act and compensation for the wrongfully incarcerated, and on economic development in the district.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney who served in the Illinois House for the 34th District from 2012 to 2018 and earlier worked as a budget analyst and Appropriations Director for Senate President Emil Jones Jr.

candidates.name: Christine McGovern
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign lists local parental control in education, support for small businesses and fiscal responsibility on pensions and the state budget, support for law enforcement, and more resources for mental health and drug addiction as priorities.
candidates.priorCareer: Owner of a real estate company who previously worked in public and private schools in the Chicago area and was twice elected to the Annie Keller Gifted School Local School Council.

candidates.name: Frances Ann Hurley
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign lists three priorities: seniors (property tax relief, lower prescription drug costs), first responders (access to mental health services and suicide prevention resources), and affordability (rising costs of groceries, utilities and housing).
candidates.priorCareer: State representative for the 35th District from 2013 to 2023, then a member of the Illinois Labor Relations Board; earlier an aide to 19th Ward aldermen and a project manager at the Cook County Sheriff's Office.

candidates.name: David A. Dewar
candidates.runningOn: He says Springfield has a spending problem rather than a revenue problem and proposes a yearly outside forensic audit of state finances, repeal of the SAFE-T Act, support for police, and same-day paper ballots; he names illegal immigration as the district's most pressing issue.
candidates.priorCareer: Independent retirement specialist who founded Tax-Free Retirement Solutions in 2010 after working in real estate, mortgage brokerage and life insurance, and served 10 years as an election judge in the 19th Ward.

candidates.name: Mary Gill
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign lists public safety, small business support, education, advocacy for people with disabilities, women's healthcare, and workers' rights as her priorities.
candidates.priorCareer: Former executive director of the Mount Greenwood Community and Business Association and former special education teacher; appointed to the 35th District seat in March 2023 and elected in 2024.

candidates.name: David Sheppard
candidates.runningOn: His campaign commitments are supporting law enforcement and cracking down on crime, stopping tax hikes, rolling back automatic gas tax increases and capping property taxes, and focusing schools on academics, parental involvement and support for children with special needs.
candidates.priorCareer: Spent 28 years in law enforcement in corrections, patrol and investigations, rising to chief of the Robbins Police Department, and serves on the Evergreen Park School District 124 board.

candidates.name: Rick Ryan
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site highlights supporting a woman's right to choose, union backing, and fighting for property tax relief.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney practicing in Oak Lawn for more than 30 years and former officer of the Southwest Bar Association; earlier worked as a union concrete laborer.

candidates.name: Xiaoli "Alice" Hu
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign lists four goals: strong neighborhoods, safe streets, lower taxes, and smarter government. She frames her candidacy around common-sense leadership, transparent government, and protecting taxpayers, and describes herself as a business leader and an independent voice rather than a career politician.
candidates.priorCareer: Small business owner who was the Republican nominee for this same seat in 2022, losing to Bridget Degnen.

candidates.name: Elizabeth Granato
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign says she will focus on protecting health care access, reducing the cost of living, and making sure large corporations and the wealthy do not shift their tax obligations onto the middle class. She points to her county government experience in procurement, budgets, federal funding streams, and health care systems as preparation for the job.
candidates.priorCareer: Bureau chief of the Cook County Bureau of Asset Management (on leave to run), with about 15 years in public service; previously served on a CPS local school council and a North River mental health services governing commission.

candidates.name: Aasi Siddique
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.

candidates.name: Josina Morita
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists justice reform, an environmental justice policy for the county, health equity, language access, small business and housing investment, transit expansion, and veterans funding as its issue areas. It also emphasizes passing balanced budgets without new taxes during her first term.
candidates.priorCareer: Urban planner and nonprofit leader for more than 20 years before joining the board, and the first Asian American woman to serve on it.

candidates.name: Miranda E. Hernandez
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign lists five priorities: improving maternal health outcomes, funding law enforcement and public safety initiatives, helping homeowners with property tax appeals, expanding small business access to grant funding, and providing recreational opportunities in the forest preserves.
candidates.priorCareer: Attorney who served as counsel to the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee and as a political appointee at the U.S. Department of Justice, then as deputy director of legislative affairs at the Cook County State's Attorney's Office, where she now works in criminal appeals.

candidates.name: Richard Nolan
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.
candidates.priorCareer: Former Riverdale village trustee and former vice president of the Riverdale School District 133 board who ran as the Republican candidate for Thornton Township supervisor in 2025; he was unopposed in the March 2026 Republican primary for this seat.

candidates.name: Kisha E. McCaskill
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists public health and human services, public safety and justice reform, transportation and infrastructure, economic development, affordable housing, and transparent budgeting as her focus areas. In 2026 campaign coverage she has pointed to high property taxes, the absence of a trauma center in south suburban Cook County, and expanding housing and affordable health care in the Southland.
candidates.priorCareer: Executive director of the Harvey Park District from 2015 until her January 2025 appointment, and a former schoolteacher, with a PhD in public administration and organizational leadership.

candidates.name: Alma E. Anaya
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site describes her work as organizing community fairs and workshops on women's health, youth employment, veterans' affairs and immigrants' rights, and providing policy research on issues facing the district. Her official office site highlights immigration legal defense funding, public health access, and protecting school-based clinics; she chairs the board's Labor Committee. No 2026-specific platform is posted.
candidates.priorCareer: Before her 2018 election she was director of administration for the 7th District office under then-Commissioner Jesus 'Chuy' Garcia, overseeing constituent services and the district budget, and holds a master's in public administration from UIC.

candidates.name: Ramona Bonilla-Anaiel
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.
candidates.priorCareer: Chicago Public Schools employee who served as an SEIU executive board member and chief union steward until the union board removed her in March 2025, and who filed as the Republican candidate for this seat in 2022 before being removed from that ballot.

candidates.name: Jessica Vasquez
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists protecting Cook County Health and expanding dental services in the district, property tax relief including help with appeals and exemptions, workers' and tenants' rights, pretrial fairness under the SAFE-T Act, maintaining sanctuary protections, and expanding the forest preserves. At her appointment she said she would focus on reforming property assessments and widening CountyCare and CareLink eligibility.
candidates.priorCareer: Chief of staff to 35th Ward Ald. Carlos Ramirez-Rosa and earlier a development associate at the Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights.

candidates.name: Jon Luers
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.
candidates.priorCareer: Software engineer (Northwestern BS and MS) from Chicago's O'Hare neighborhood who was the Republican nominee for Illinois Senate 10th District in 2022 and 2024, losing both times to Robert Martwick.

candidates.name: Maggie Trevor
candidates.runningOn: Her campaign site lists access to health care, stewardship of the environment and forest preserves, transportation improvements, and equitable taxes with efficient use of tax dollars as her priorities. Her re-election statement says federal changes to Medicaid and the ACA, public transit funding, and the EPA will strain county health services, transit projects, and local environmental protections, and calls for fiscal responsibility and better coordination of county services.
candidates.priorCareer: University of Chicago PhD in political science who taught at the University of Iowa, then spent two decades as a health care market researcher (Kaiser Foundation Health Plan, Blue Shield of California, vice president of YouGov Healthcare) before founding Trevor Research Services in Rolling Meadows in 2014.

candidates.name: Drake Warren
candidates.runningOn: His campaign site lists six planks: protecting health care (strengthening Cook County Health and CountyCare), fairness in property taxes, lowering the cost of living by expanding housing supply, standing up to federal actions including immigration enforcement and data sharing, restorative justice, and an open and ethical county government. In coverage he has also proposed ethics rules barring officials from voting on matters tied to their employers and exploring land value or split-rate taxation.
candidates.priorCareer: Industrial engineer and West Monroe consultant who spent about a decade as a community organizer on housing, health care access, and environmental restoration; a first-time candidate who served on the Chicago Growth Project steering committee.

candidates.name: Charles Spizzirri
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.

candidates.name: John P. Daley
candidates.runningOn: Has not published a platform for this race that we could find.
candidates.priorCareer: Former school teacher and insurance broker who served in the Illinois House (1985 to 1989) and Illinois Senate (1989 to 1992) before joining the county board in February 1992; he chairs the board's Finance Committee.
